sentences.zh: 《指环王》。

sentences.en: Well, Tolkien's initial choices are always bad because we said in the last podcast that the elves were going to be gnomes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，托尔金最初的选择总是很糟糕，因为我们在上期播客中说过，精灵们原本打算叫侏儒（gnomes）。

sentences.en: But also there's a character called Aragorn who, you know, not to spoil it for our listeners, but Aragorn is basically King Arthur, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但还有一个角色叫阿拉贡，你知道，不是要给听众剧透，但阿拉贡基本上就是亚瑟王，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's an exiled king who's trying to get, he's got this sword, which is the badge of his kingship.
sentences.zh: 他是一个流亡的国王，正试图夺回……他有这把剑，这是他王权的标志。

sentences.en: Nick Scalibur kind of.
sentences.zh: 有点像石中剑（Excalibur）。

sentences.en: Wants to reclaim his throne.
sentences.zh: 想要夺回他的王位。

sentences.en: But he's first introduced to our heroes as a mysterious ranger, a hooded figure, a man of the sort of the hills and stuff called Strider.
sentences.zh: 但他最初是以一名神秘游侠的身份被介绍给我们的英雄们的，一个戴兜帽的身影，一个来自山间之类地方的人，名叫“大步佬”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But Tolkien's initial name for him was Trotter.
sentences.zh: 但托尔金最初给他起的名字是“特罗特”。

sentences.en: So if they were called Bingo and Trotter, Bingo and Trotter, it would have been much less successful.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们叫“宾戈”和“特罗特”，宾戈和特罗特，那这部作品的成功程度肯定会大打折扣。

sentences.en: Bingo and Trotter meet the gnomes.
sentences.zh: 宾戈和特罗特遇见了地精。

sentences.en: But also the kind of the great villain who essentially is a kind of Satan figure in Lord of the Rings is Sauron, Sauron the Great, Sauron the Terrible.
sentences.zh: 但同样，在《指环王》中本质上属于撒旦式人物的那个大反派是索伦，索伦大帝，恐怖的索伦。

sentences.en: And this is a figure who has already appeared in, you know, Tolkien's collection of myths and legends in which he initially appears as a cat.
sentences.zh: 这是一个已经在托尔金的神话传说集中出现过的人物，他最初是以一只猫的形象出现的。

sentences.en: Do you know that?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I didn't know he appeared as a cat.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他曾以猫的形象出现过。

sentences.en: No, I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 不，我不知道。

sentences.en: Initially, the initial name for Sauron was Tavildo, the Prince of Cats, like kind of old possum.
sentences.zh: 最初，索伦的名字叫塔维尔多，猫之王子，就像老负鼠那样。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, yes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，确实是这样。

sentences.en: But he got there in the end, to be fair to Tolkien.
sentences.zh: 但说句公道话，托尔金最终还是把名字定下来了。

sentences.en: Well, he does get there in the end because the names are absolutely fundamental.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他最终确实定下来了，因为名字绝对是根本性的。

sentences.en: And once you've heard the names, you know basically where they're coming from.
sentences.zh: 一旦你听到了这些名字，你基本上就知道它们源自何处了。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实做到了。

sentences.en: So, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: He does, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 他确实做到了，绝对的。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是啊。

sentences.en: So, he sets off.
sentences.zh: 所以，他出发了。

sentences.en: So, we should just, I suppose, very quickly give the plot of Lord of the Rings, shouldn't we?
sentences.zh: 所以，我想我们应该非常快速地讲一下《指环王》的剧情，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's quite...
sentences.zh: 我是说，这相当……

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Imagine condensing that in a minute.
sentences.zh: 想象一下在一分钟内浓缩完这些内容。

sentences.en: So, basically, the ring that Bilbo took off Gollum turns out to be a ring that is the key to the fate of the whole of Middle Earth.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，比尔博从咕噜那里拿走的戒指，结果成了决定整个中土世界命运的关键。

sentences.en: So, the whole world of mortal men and dwarves and elves and also these kind of twisted, tortured elves who've become orcs, who are kind of monsters.
sentences.zh: 所以，整个凡人、矮人、精灵的世界，还有那些变成了半兽人的扭曲、受折磨的精灵，也就是那些怪物。

sentences.en: And whoever controls the ring, basically, will have mastery.
sentences.zh: 而且谁控制了戒指，基本上就拥有了统治权。

sentences.en: And Sauron in the distant land of Mordor is plotting a great military conquest of the world.
sentences.zh: 而远在魔多之地的索伦正在策划一场伟大的世界军事征服。

sentences.en: But to absolutely secure his victory, he needs to get this ring.
sentences.zh: 但为了绝对确保胜利，他需要得到这枚戒指。

sentences.en: And Frodo, Bilbo's nephew, Gandalf the wizard who had originally sent Bilbo on the quest, Aragorn, who you mentioned, various other hobbits,
sentences.zh: 还有弗罗多，比尔博的侄子，最初派遣比尔博去冒险的巫师甘道夫，你提到的阿拉贡，以及其他各种霍比特人，

sentences.en: a dwarf, an elf, another man.
sentences.zh: 一个矮人，一个精灵，另一个人。

sentences.en: I mean, it was all this...
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真是……

sentences.en: It's impossible to describe it without getting the sense of hackles going up from people who hate this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果不让那些讨厌这类东西的人感到反感，是无法描述它的。

sentences.en: But anyway, basically, they decide that the only thing that they can do is to destroy the ring, which Sauron...
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，基本上，他们决定唯一能做的就是摧毁戒指，而索伦……

sentences.en: It never crosses Sauron's mind that they would want to do that because the ring is the key to great power.
sentences.zh: 索伦从未想过他们会想要那样做，因为戒指是巨大力量的关键。

sentences.en: Because it's the ultimate weapon.
sentences.zh: 因为它是终极武器。

sentences.en: The idea that you would want to get rid of the ring, that you would want to essentially to kind of celebrate your weakness, is impossible for Sauron to comprehend.
sentences.zh: 想要摆脱戒指，本质上想要赞美自己的软弱，这种想法对索伦来说是无法理解的。

sentences.en: And in the end, Frodo, who is, you know, I mean, he's a hobbit, very short, not the kind of person who anyone would think would be a great warrior.
sentences.zh: 最后，弗罗多，你知道，我是说，他是个霍比特人，非常矮小，不是那种会被人认为是伟大战士的人。

sentences.en: He ends up doing this great thing.
sentences.zh: 他最终完成了这件伟大的事情。

sentences.en: He destroys the ring.
sentences.zh: 他摧毁了戒指。

sentences.en: Well, or does he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者说他真的摧毁了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, this is...
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是……

sentences.en: Or does it?
sentences.zh: 或者说它真的被摧毁了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, okay.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧。

sentences.en: That's an interesting question itself.
sentences.zh: 这本身就是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: So the great criticism of The Lord of the Rings for people who hate it is that it is silly and childish and escapiSt. And I think we can safely debunk the escapism, Tom, because
sentences.zh: 所以，讨厌《指环王》的人对它的最大批评是它愚蠢、幼稚且逃避现实。汤姆，我认为我们可以放心地驳斥这种逃避现实的说法，因为

sentences.en: we talked in the first podcast about the searing impact of World War I.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一期播客中谈到了第一次世界大战的剧烈影响。

sentences.en: Tolkien starts writing
sentences.zh: 托尔金开始撰写

sentences.en: The Lord of the Rings just before the outbreak of the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 《指环王》是在第二次世界大战爆发前夕。

sentences.en: So we're talking late
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是1937、38、39年
末期。

sentences.en: So the storm clouds are very much, I mean, to use my favourite cliche, the storm clouds are very much gathering.
sentences.zh: 所以风暴云层非常……我是说，用我最喜欢的陈词滥调，风暴云层确实正在聚集。

sentences.en: In the first part, I talked about this chapter, the Council of Elrond, which is held at a place
sentences.zh: 在第一部分，我谈到了这一章，“埃尔隆德会议”，它是在一个叫

sentences.en: called Rivendell, where the Fellowship of the Ring, the group of people who have come together
sentences.zh: 瑞文戴尔的地方举行的，护戒使者，也就是聚集在一起

sentences.en: to go on this mission, so Gandalf and Frodo and the Hobbits and the Elf and the Dwarf and so on and Aragorn.
sentences.zh: 去执行这项任务的那群人，甘道夫、弗罗多、霍比特人、精灵、矮人等等，还有阿拉贡。

sentences.en: They decide that they're going to go.
sentences.zh: 他们决定出发。

sentences.en: And the only way that they can defeat Sauron, this kind of great menace that is brewing in the East, is to throw away the ring and to throw it into this volcano.
sentences.zh: 而他们击败索伦——这个在东方酝酿的巨大威胁——的唯一方法，就是扔掉戒指，把它扔进这座火山里。

sentences.en: And he is writing that chapter in September 1939.
sentences.zh: 而他在1939年9月写到了那一章。

sentences.en: So all the various people sitting around saying, how are we going to defeat this terrible evil?
sentences.zh: 所以所有坐在周围的人都在说，我们该如何击败这个可怕的邪恶？

sentences.en: How are we going to do it?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么做？

sentences.en: It's clearly, I mean, it would be incomprehensible if it's not, you know, the news of the war isn't the backdrop to that.
sentences.zh: 很明显，我是说，如果战争的消息不是背景，那是不可思议的。

sentences.en: Well, I was about to say the device of the ring.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我正要说戒指这个设定。

sentences.en: So magic rings are ten a penny in kind of Norse myths and legends and fairy stories and folk stories.
sentences.zh: 所以魔法戒指在北欧神话、传说、童话和民间故事里多如牛毛。

sentences.en: But the ring is such a brilliant creation.
sentences.zh: 但戒指是一个如此天才的创造。

sentences.en: I mean, even if you despise Tolkien, the ring is a very sophisticated kind of literary device.
sentences.zh: 我是说，即使你鄙视托尔金，戒指也是一种非常复杂的文学手段。

sentences.en: Because the ring is not just the key to power.
sentences.zh: 因为戒指不仅仅是权力的关键。

sentences.en: It's not just the ultimate weapon.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是终极武器。

sentences.en: But it is a symbol of corruption, of technological and sort of intellectual and moral corruption.
sentences.zh: 它还是腐败的象征，是技术、智力和道德腐败的象征。

sentences.en: So the more you use it, the more you become addicted to it.
sentences.zh: 所以你用得越多，你就越会对它上瘾。

sentences.en: And over time, you lose your, as it were, your humanity.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，你会失去你的，可以说是，人性。

sentences.en: If you're a hobbit, your hobbitness, the more you are exposed to it.
sentences.zh: 如果你是霍比特人，你接触它越多，就会失去你的“霍比特性”。

sentences.en: So it's like a combination of, the ring means power, and it kind of means mastery.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像一种结合，戒指意味着力量，也意味着某种统治。

sentences.en: It means dominion over other people, but also over the natural world.
sentences.zh: 它意味着对他人的支配，也意味着对自然世界的支配。

sentences.en: But it also is a kind of symbol of hubris.
sentences.zh: 但它也是一种傲慢的象征。

sentences.en: And it also kind of brings out the evil that is in you.
sentences.zh: 它也激发了你内心深处的邪恶。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, we are talking about the mid 20th century, the age of concentration camps, of totalitarianism, of dictatorship, all these things.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，我们谈论的是20世纪中期，集中营、极权主义、独裁统治的时代，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: The ring is very clearly, the ring would not have been invented by a mid-Victorian writer, maybe even by an Edwardian writer.
sentences.zh: 戒指非常明显，它不会是由维多利亚时代中期的作家发明的，甚至可能不是由爱德华时代的作家发明的。

sentences.en: I think, but it feels to me like, I mean, Tolkien is writing the
sentences.zh: 我想，但这给我的感觉是，我是说，托尔金在写

sentences.en: Lord of the Rings at the same time that people like, let's say, William Golding, he's going to go on and write the Lord of the Flies in the middle of the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 《指环王》的同时，像威廉·戈尔丁这样的人，他后来在1950年代中期写了《蝇王》。

sentences.en: The other people are wrestling with questions about evil and power, and thinking, you know, if we bomb the Germans, are we as bad as them?
sentences.zh: 其他人也在与关于邪恶和权力的疑问作斗争，思考着，你知道，如果我们轰炸德国人，我们是否和他们一样坏？

sentences.en: These kinds of issues are absolutely bound up with the ring, the device of the ring.
sentences.zh: 这些问题与戒指，即戒指这一设定，是绝对紧密相连的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Tolkien writes about this quite a lot to his son, Christopher, who was training with the RAF.
sentences.zh: 所以托尔金给他的儿子克里斯托弗写了很多关于这方面的信，当时他正在英国皇家空军受训。

sentences.en: And this is in the context of the RAF launching bombing campaigns over Germany.
sentences.zh: 这正是在英国皇家空军对德国发动轰炸行动的背景下。

sentences.en: And Tolkien is very, very against this, very hostile to this.
sentences.zh: 而托尔金非常、非常反对这一点，对这种做法非常敌视。

sentences.en: And he frames it specifically in terms of Lord of the Rings, which he's writing as these bombing campaigns are going on.
sentences.zh: 他专门用《指环王》的语境来阐述这一点，而他在写这本书时，这些轰炸行动正在进行。

sentences.en: So he says, you can't fight the enemy with his own ring without turning into an enemy.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，你不能用敌人的戒指去对抗敌人，否则你自己也会变成敌人。

sentences.en: And he says of the bombing campaigns that it's an ultimately evil job, for we are attempting to conquer Sauron with the ring, and we shall, it seems, succeed.
sentences.zh: 他谈到轰炸行动时说，这是一项终极的邪恶工作，因为我们正试图用戒指去征服索伦，而且看来我们将会成功。

sentences.en: But the penalty is, as you will know, to breed new Saurons.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所知，代价是培育出新的索伦。

sentences.en: So essentially, the Lord of the Rings is consciously written as a mirror that is being held up to the moral dilemmas that confront the Allies in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，《指环王》是有意识地作为一面镜子，映照出盟军在第二次世界大战中所面临的道德困境。

sentences.en: How much evil can you inflict in the name of defeating evil?
sentences.zh: 以击败邪恶的名义，你可以施加多少邪恶？

sentences.en: And at what point does doing that mean that you yourself become evil?
sentences.zh: 在什么程度上，这样做意味着你自己也变成了邪恶？

sentences.en: And I think that in that sense, and this is what I absolutely didn't see when I read it as a child,
sentences.zh: 我认为从这个意义上说，这是我小时候读它时绝对没有看到的，

sentences.en: but it seems very clear to me, the Lord of the Rings is the great novel on the horrors of the mid-20th century.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说现在非常清楚，《指环王》是关于20世纪中期恐怖的伟大长篇小说。

sentences.en: And it spans all shades and kinds.
sentences.zh: 它涵盖了各种阴影和类型。

sentences.en: So there's Orwell is there as well.
sentences.zh: 所以奥威尔也在其中。

sentences.en: So there's a very, very kind of big brother quality to Sauron and his lieutenants.
sentences.zh: 所以索伦和他的副官们有一种非常、非常强烈的“老大哥”特质。

sentences.en: The symbol of Sauron is a giant eye that is surveying everything and will see you no matter where you hide.
sentences.zh: 索伦的象征是一只巨大的眼睛，它监视着一切，无论你躲在哪里都能看到你。

sentences.en: I mean, again, that's a very Orwellian image, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这又是一个非常奥威尔式的意象，不是吗？

sentences.en: And the orcs, they're always kind of telling on each other, you know, I'll give your name and number
sentences.zh: 而半兽人，他们总是互相告密，你知道，我会把你的名字和编号

sentences.en: to the Nazgul, who are the kind of the ring race, the figures of terror who patrol the sky.
sentences.zh: 交给戒灵，也就是那些戒指幽灵，那些在天空中巡逻的恐怖化身。

sentences.en: So that's, it's even that again, just as I'm sure the ghost of the Red Baron haunts these terrifying,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使是这一点，就像我相信红男爵的幽灵萦绕在这些恐怖之物上一样，

sentences.en: so the ring race, they're nine kind of cloaked figures whose faces you never see.
sentences.zh: 戒灵，他们是九个披着斗篷的身影，你永远看不见他们的脸。

sentences.en: They're just kind of images of the Grim Reaper, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，他们只是死神的形象。

sentences.en: And they ride on kind of pterosaurs.
sentences.zh: 他们骑在某种翼龙上。

sentences.en: And Tolkien was actually asked, are they pterodactyls?
sentences.zh: 托尔金实际上被问到，它们是翼手龙吗？

sentences.en: And he said, no, but they're pterodactylish,
sentences.zh: 他说，不，但它们很像翼手龙，

sentences.en: which I love.
sentences.zh: 这一点我很喜欢。

sentences.en: Very precise.
sentences.zh: 非常精确。

sentences.en: But so one of the things at the end is that after Frodo has thrown the ring into the,
sentences.zh: 但结局的一件事是，在弗罗多把戒指扔进……之后，

sentences.en: where I'm giving all kinds of spoilers away, but what the hell, people know this, the quest does, to that extent, succeed.
sentences.zh: 我在这里剧透了一切，但管他呢，人们都知道这一点，任务在那个程度上成功了。

sentences.en: Frodo doesn't throw it in time.
sentences.zh: 弗罗多没有及时把它扔进去。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: We won't give away how and why it happens, but the ring is destroyed and Magdum erupts and Gandalf gets on an eagle and flies across Mordor and rescues him and Sam
sentences.zh: 我们不会剧透它是如何以及为什么发生的，但戒指被摧毁了，末日火山爆发了，甘道夫骑着巨鹰飞过魔多，救出了他和山姆，

sentences.en: and bring them back.
sentences.zh: 并把他们带了回来。

sentences.en: And people say, well, why didn't they just do that in the first place?
sentences.zh: 人们说，好吧，为什么他们不一开始就那样做呢？

sentences.en: Well, the answer is very clear.
sentences.zh: 嗯，答案非常明确。

sentences.en: The Nazgul on their pterodactyls are essentially a kind of air defence system.
sentences.zh: 骑着翼手龙的戒灵本质上是一种防空系统。

sentences.en: You can't penetrate it.
sentences.zh: 你无法渗透它。

sentences.en: And until they've been destroyed, which they do once the ring gets destroyed.
sentences.zh: 直到它们被摧毁，而这在戒指被摧毁后就发生了。

sentences.en: That's a very clear, you know, clearly how you defend territory from aerial intrusion is absolutely a part of it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常清晰的，你知道，如何防御领土免受空中入侵，绝对是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And all the more so because Tolkien was an air raid warden.
sentences.zh: 而且更是因为托尔金曾是一名空袭监视员。

sentences.en: Oh, was he?
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.en: He was.
sentences.zh: 他是。

sentences.en: That's a very nice...
sentences.zh: 那真是个非常好的……

sentences.en: He was.
sentences.zh: 他是。

sentences.en: So he was an air raid warden in North Oxford.
sentences.zh: 所以他是北牛津的一名空袭监视员。

sentences.en: And again, in the echoes of the Blitz, the echo of the aerial war, Arthur, Lord of the Rings.

sentences.en: I don't think, well, I think the very fact of the Amazon series, so this new series, which has given us the peg for where they've made a deliberate attempt, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 我不认为，嗯，我认为亚马逊系列剧的事实本身，也就是这个新系列，它给了我们一个切入点，他们不是做出了故意的尝试吗？

sentences.en: They've got black hobbits.
sentences.zh: 他们有黑人霍比特人。

sentences.en: Well, they've got Lenny Henry, who is probably the most famous black West Midlander in England.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们有兰尼·亨利（Lenny Henry），他可能是英国最著名的黑人西米德兰兹人。

sentences.en: So that seems to me entirely appropriate.
sentences.zh: 所以这在我看来完全是恰当的。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems entirely with the grain of going with the grain of everything that Tolkien's ambitions would have been, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这完全符合托尔金的抱负。

sentences.en: Well, people who are Tolkien critics, who defend Tolkien, sort of Tolkien scholars, will often say he created a world that was by definition multicultural.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那些托尔金的批评者，那些捍卫托尔金的人，也就是所谓的托尔金学者，经常会说他创造的世界本质上就是多元文化的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, different languages.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，不同的语言。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, the theme of the Lord of the Rings is different species, I guess, working together.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，《指环王》的主题就是不同的物种，我想，是共同协作。

sentences.en: Yeah, the three peoples.
sentences.zh: 是的，三个种族。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there's no doubt that Tolkien is a product of empire, that he's read Rider-Haggard, that he never questions these things.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为毫无疑问，托尔金是帝国的产物，他读过莱德·哈格德（Rider-Haggard）的作品，他从不质疑这些事情。

sentences.en: But why would he?
sentences.zh: 但他为什么要质疑呢？

sentences.en: I mean, most people don't in the 1930s and 1940s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在20世纪30年代和40年代，大多数人都不质疑。

sentences.en: It seems to me completely absurd to expect Tolkien to be a man of, I mean, he was barely even a man of the 20th century intellectually.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，期望托尔金成为一个……我的意思是，他在知识层面上甚至勉强算是一个20世纪的人，期望他成为那样的人是完全荒谬的。

sentences.en: I think the weird thing about him is the way in which, again and again,
sentences.zh: 我认为关于他最奇怪的事情是，他一次又一次地，

sentences.en: he's so reactionary that he ends up becoming almost, by our standards, progressive.
sentences.zh: 表现得如此反动，以至于按照我们的标准，他最终几乎变得进步了。

sentences.en: It's kind of like- So the environmentalism.
sentences.zh: 这有点像——比如环保主义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's kind of like fascists ending up like communists.
sentences.zh: 这有点像法西斯最终变成了共产主义者。

sentences.en: It's that same kind of weird, I suppose, like a ring, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一种同样的奇怪，我想，就像一枚戒指，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's, you know, very nice image, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的比喻，汤姆。

sentences.en: Do you think, I mean, his book has proved enormously successful, far more successful than, so his critics said at first, I mean, they were saying in the 1970s, even in the 1980s,
sentences.zh: 你认为，我的意思是，他的书被证明是非常成功的，远比他的批评者最初所说的要成功得多，我的意思是，他们在20世纪70年代，甚至80年代还在说，

sentences.en: it will eventually be forgotten and is merely diversion for teenagers.
sentences.zh: 它最终会被遗忘，仅仅是青少年的消遣。

sentences.en: That clearly, you know, has not worked out because it's proved enormously successful.
sentences.zh: 显然，你知道，情况并非如此，因为它被证明是非常成功的。

sentences.en: But do you think it will continue to be one of the books that people read and reread?
sentences.zh: 但你认为它会继续成为人们阅读和重读的书籍之一吗？

sentences.en: You know, are people going to be reading it in the 22nd century?
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们在22世纪还会读它吗？

sentences.en: I'd have thought so, because there's clearly something about it that tugs you in.
sentences.zh: 我想会的，因为书中显然有什么东西在吸引着你。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an incredibly well-told story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个讲述得非常好的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: Aside from anything else.
sentences.zh: 撇开其他一切不谈。

sentences.en: It's an incredibly exciting adventure story with few parallels.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其精彩的冒险故事，几乎没有同类作品可以媲美。

sentences.en: Tom, I think it's fair to say that we could talk, there's so many things we haven't talked about.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为公平地说，我们可以谈论的还有很多，有很多我们还没有谈到的事情。

sentences.en: So we haven't talked about extremes of women.
sentences.zh: 比如我们还没有谈到女性的极端表现。

sentences.en: We haven't talked about Sam as our First World War Batman.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有谈到山姆作为我们一战时期的勤务兵（Batman）。

sentences.en: We haven't talked about
sentences.zh: 我们还没有谈到

sentences.en: Gollum as much as I was hoping to, basically because we're Lord of the Rings nerds, and we could have bored on for hours, couldn't we?
sentences.zh: 咕噜（Gollum），虽然我本来希望多谈谈，主要是因为我们是《指环王》的死忠粉，我们可以没完没了地聊上几个小时，不是吗？

sentences.en: And we should confess at this stage that many years ago, we had Lord of the Rings marathon where we watched the extended editions of the
sentences.zh: 我们应该在现阶段承认，多年前，我们举办过一次《指环王》马拉松，我们观看了加长版的

sentences.en: films together with takeaways, and our respective wives refused to join us.
sentences.zh: 电影，配着外卖，而我们的妻子拒绝加入我们。

sentences.en: And that tells its own story, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这本身就说明了一切，不是吗？

sentences.en: But on that bombshell, I think we should probably let, because we've been talking for over an hour, and we should probably let people go about the rest of their lives.
sentences.zh: 但带着这个重磅消息，我想我们可能应该让大家去过他们的生活了，因为我们已经聊了一个多小时了。

sentences.en: But Tom, since we started with The Beginning of the Hobbit, I think we should end with the end of The Lord of the Rings.
sentences.zh: 但是汤姆，既然我们是从《霍比特人》的开头开始的，我想我们应该以《指环王》的结尾来结束。

sentences.en: Would you like me to give another of my nice readings?
sentences.zh: 你想让我再来一段精彩的朗读吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, like your Larkin.
sentences.zh: 好啊，就像你读拉金（Larkin）那样。

sentences.en: Like my Larkin, exactly.
sentences.zh: 就像我读拉金，没错。

sentences.en: People were moved to tears by that.
sentences.zh: 人们都被那段朗读感动得热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: Or indeed, my readings from my own books, Adventures in Time, which are available right now.
sentences.zh: 或者，确实，朗读我自己的书《时间冒险》（Adventures in Time），现在就可以买到。

sentences.en: And actually, J.R.R.
sentences.zh: And actually, J.R.R.

sentences.en: Tolkien is the opening character of my book about the First World War, which, if you have children, or you know children, or you've ever been a child, I advise you to buy
sentences.zh: 托尔金是我那本关于第一次世界大战的书的开篇人物，如果你有孩子，或者认识孩子，或者你曾经是个孩子，我建议你

sentences.en: forthwith.
sentences.zh: 立即购买。

sentences.en: And of course, he's also a key figure in my chapter on the Second World War of Dominion, which I will say, strongly recommend that you buy.
sentences.zh: 当然，他也是我关于第二次世界大战的《统治》（Dominion）一书章节中的关键人物，我强烈建议你购买。

sentences.en: J.R.R.
sentences.zh: J.R.R.

sentences.en: Tolkien was a great believer in commercial self-promotion, wasn't he, Tom?
sentences.zh: 托尔金是一个坚定的商业自我推销信徒，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: He truly was.
sentences.zh: 他确实是。

sentences.en: Well, he appeared in a calendar.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他出现在了一本挂历上。

sentences.en: Yes, he did.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实出现了。

sentences.en: But he's sitting, he's fully encased in tweed, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他坐着，全身裹在粗花呢里，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's sitting next to an oak.
sentences.zh: 他坐在一棵橡树旁边。

sentences.en: I think that's a calendar we could do.
sentences.zh: 我想那是一本我们可以做的挂历。

sentences.en: Yes, he's dressed as Stanley Baldwin.
sentences.zh: 是的，他打扮得像斯坦利·鲍德温（Stanley Baldwin）。

sentences.en: Okay, here we go.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: At last, the three companions turned away, and never again looking back, they rode slowly
sentences.zh: 终于，三位同伴转过身去，再也没有回头，他们缓慢地骑马

sentences.en: homewards, and they spoke no word to one another until they came back to the shire, but each had great comfort in his friends on the long grey road.
sentences.zh: 回家，一路上他们一言不发，直到回到夏尔，但在漫长灰暗的道路上，朋友的陪伴给了他们极大的安慰。

sentences.en: At last, they rode over the downs and took the east road, and then Merry and Pippin rode on to Buckland, and already they were singing again as they went.
sentences.zh: 终于，他们翻过丘陵，走上了东大道，然后梅里和皮平骑马前往巴克兰，他们一路上又开始唱歌了。

sentences.en: But Sam turned to buy water, and so came back up the hill as day was ending once more.
sentences.zh: 但山姆转向拜沃特（Bywater），随着白昼再次结束，他回到了山上。

sentences.en: And he went on, and there was yellow light and fire within, and the evening meal was ready, and he was expected.
sentences.zh: 他继续前行，屋里透出黄色的灯光和炉火，晚饭已经准备好了，大家都在等他。

sentences.zh: 罗斯把他拉了进去，让他坐在椅子上，把小埃莉诺放在他的膝盖上。

sentences.en: He drew a deep breath.
sentences.zh: 他深吸了一口气。

sentences.en: Well, I'm back, he said.
sentences.zh: “嗯，我回来了，”他说。
